 # Blocky Adirondack Chair

A modern, slab-style Adirondack chair cut entirely from one sheet thickness of plywood on a CNC router.

## Inputs (editable in run mode)
- **Thickness** – sheet thickness (default 19.05 mm / 3/4")
- **Seat_Width** – clear width between the side runners (default 560 mm)
- **Back_Angle** – back lean from vertical in degrees (default 24)
- **Arm_Height** – top of the arms above the floor (default 600 mm)
- **Leg Sweep** – how far the front legs lean back from vertical in degrees (default 20)

## Parts (15)
- 2 × side runners (sloped seat support, toe rests on the floor)
- 1 × front apron
- 2 × seat panels
- 2 × back panels
- 1 × lower back batten (behind the back panels, between the runners)
- 1 × upper back batten (under the arms, behind the back)
- 2 × front legs (swept back, outboard of the runners)
- 2 × rear posts (outboard of the runners, carry the upper batten)
- 2 × arms (rounded front corners)

## Assembly
1. Screw the front legs and rear posts to the outside faces of the runners.
2. Screw the apron across the front ends of the runners.
3. Screw the lower back batten between the runners, then fix the back panels to it.
4. Lay the upper back batten across the tops of the rear posts and screw the back panels to its front edge.
5. Screw the seat panels down onto the runners' seat slope.
6. Screw the arms down onto the front legs and the upper batten.

Use exterior-grade plywood and stainless or coated deck screws.
